Design of 1 ‑Phosphanorbornene Derivatives as Chiral
Organocatalysts for Enantioselective (4 + 2) Annulation Reactions of
γ‑Benzyl Allenoates
Siming Jia, Mengmeng Ma, Er-Qing Li, * Zheng Duan, * and Franc ̧is Mathey
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 3337 −3342 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: Two novel diastereoisomeric P-chirogenic phosphine catalysts, i.e., JiaPhos, which can be easily derived from
inexpensive and commercially available starting materials in ﬁve chemical operations (totally 4.16g scale), are introduced. To our
delight, the JiaPhos catalysts display good performance in enantioselective (4 + 2) annulations involving 3-methylene-2-oxindoles
and γ-benzyl allenoates, providing a wide range of 3,3 ′-spirocyclic oxindoles with good e ﬃciency and enantioselectivity.
P
hosphine-catalyzed reactions o ﬀer a very powerful tool for
the synthesis of structurally diverse optically active organic
building blocks. 1 As a result, the design of e ﬃcient chiral
phosphine catalysts has attracted much attention. 2 In the past
decades, many types of chiral phosphines have been developed
by Lu, 3 Zhao,4 Huang,5 Fu,6 Zhang,7 and other organic
chemists. 8 Although these phosphines showed excellent
catalytic activities in asymmetric phosphine catalysis, e ﬃcient
methodology for the design and synthesis of P-stereogenic
phosphines remains scarce. An early example with the
development of P-chirogenic catalysts was disclosed by the
Zhang group in 1997.
9 Subsequently, Sasai ’s group designed a
novel P-chirogenic catalyst with an o-hydroxyalkyl chelating
arm, which exhibited good performance in the aza-Morita −
Baylis−Hillman (aza-MBH) reaction.10 In 2014, Kwon and co-
workers developed a novel family of P-stereogenic [2.2.1]
bicyclic chiral phosphines, applying them in the asymmetric
installation of pyrrolines. 11 Recently, Zhang’s group reported a
novel class of cyclic phosphine-derived bifunctional phosphine
catalysts (Le-Phos), which showed high enantioselectivity in γ-
addition reactions of N-centered nucleophiles to allenoates
(Scheme 1, A).
12 As a part of our program, we set our goal to
de novo design novel P-stereogenic catalysts derived from the
1-phosphanorbornenes, in which three P −C bonds of the P-
chirogenic center are absolutely shackled. In addition, the two
alkyl groups link to the phosphorus atom that shows better
nucleophilic activity than 1-phosphanorbornadienes,
13 and
combining with a H-bonding site and multiple tunable side
chains, the de novo design of P-chirogenic catalysts (i.e.,
Jiaphos) may extend the applicative scope of asymmetric
phosphine catalysis to a greater extent ( Scheme 1 , B).
In 2003, Mathey and co-workers reported a Diels −Alder
reaction of 2 H-phospholes with trans-cinnamaldehyde.14 The
cycloaddition primarily took place at the C O bond, and only
minor C C bond adducts could be obtained. The
experimental results demonstrated that the carbonyl group of
aldehydes could compete with activated alkenes in (4 + 2)
cycloadditions. To our delight, when we applied trans-
cinnamaldehyde dimethyl acetal as a reactive substrate, the
cycloaddition completely took place at the C C bond,
aﬀording the desired compounds e ﬃciently. The phosphine
was then protected by further vulcanization. The mixture of
exo/endo-1 was obtained in a total of 61% yield, which could
be straightforwardly separated by column chromatography,
giving the exo-1 in 52% yield. Next, deprotection of exo-1 in
CH
2Cl2 at 0 °C produced the desired compound 2 (94%
yield). Two sets of diastereomeric chiral sul ﬁnyl imines 3 could
be obtained in a total of 80% yield by the condensation
reaction of compound 2 with (RS)-tert-butanesulﬁnamide. The
stereoselective addition of ArMgBr to compound 3 followed by
reduction with Raney Ni then a ﬀorded two sets of

which could be straightforwardly separated by column
chromatography. To test the practicality of this new method-
ology, a gram-scale synthesis was carried out. To our delight,
the 32.0 mmol scale reaction produced 2.16 g of ( R
p,S,RS)-5
and 2.0 g of ( Sp,R,RS)-5′ in a total of 15.6% and 14.5% yield by
ﬁve steps, thus indicating that this transformation was easy to
scale-up to gram scale without loss of e ﬃciency and selectivity
(Scheme 2 ). The absolute con ﬁgurations of the two sets of
JiaPhos catalysts were established by single-crystal X-ray
diﬀraction analysis ( 4d and 4d′).
With the P-chirogenic phosphine JiaPhos in hand, the
performance of Jia-Phos catalysts was focused on the
asymmetric catalysis. In 2013, Marinetti and Huang ’s group
reported a novel phosphine-catalyzed (4 + 2) annulation of γ-
benzyl allenoates, respectively.
15 However, the development of
enantioselective variants of these transformations has met with
very limited success. For Huang ’s (4 + 2) reaction, Lu ’s group
used NUSIOC-Phos as a catalyst, and only 39% ee was
obtained.
16 For Marinetti ’s (4 + 2) reaction, only 50% yield
and 66% ee were obtained with ( S,S)-BDPP. Thus, we chose γ-
benzyl allenoates and 3-methylene-2-oxindoles as potential
synthetic precursors to test its use in enantioselective
phosphine catalysis.

the presence of catalyst 5a aﬀorded the product 8aa in 93%
yield with 99% ee and minor (3 + 2) product 9aa (8aa:9aa =
23:1) ( Table 1 , entry 1). When ethyl acetate is used as the
solvent, we found that a similar result could be produced at 50
°C in the presence of catalyst 5a (Table 1 , entry 2). From a
green and sustainable chemistry point of view, we ﬁnally chose
ethyl acetate as the solvent. The addition of benzoic acid led to
improvements in the chemoselectivity ( Table 1, entry 3). Next,
diﬀerent JiaPhos 5a−5e catalysts were examined further, and
the catalysts 5a proved to be the best choice ( Table 1 , entries
3−7), a ﬀording the desired product in 95% yield with 99% ee
(Table 1 , entry 3). Two sets of chiral phosphines 5 and 5′,
albeit with diastere oisomeric property, possess opposite
stereochemistry at their P-chiral centers at which the covalent
bonds to the allenoates were formed, and we thus anticipated
that they might give respective 3,3 ′-spirocyclic oxindole
antipodes. To our delight, the catalyst 5a′ could also provide
the opposite 3,3 ′-spirocyclic oxindole enantiomer in 51% yield
with −98% ee ( Table 1 , entry 8). The increase of catalyst
loading could improve the yield ( Table 1 , entries 8 −10). To
further enhance the results, the screening of solvents suggested
that toluene was identi ﬁed as the solvent of choice ( Table 1 ,
entries 11 −16). The addition of benzoic acid still led to an
improvement in both chemical yield and chemoselectivity
(Table 1 entries 11 vs 17). In almost all of the catalysts 5a′−
5e′ examined, the excellent enantioselectivity could be
obtained, albeit with moderate to excellent yields ( Table 1
entries 17 −21). Remarkably, JiaPhos 5a′
promoted the
formation of 3,3 ′-spirocyclic oxindole in 95% yield as well as
−98% ee under the optimized reaction conditions ( Table 1 ,
entry 17).
With the established optimal reaction conditions in hand, we
ﬁrst explored the reaction scope in the presence of catalyst 5a,
and the results are summarized in Scheme 3. The aryl group in
6 was well tolerated, regardless of the electronic nature and
substitution pattern of the aryl moieties of the methyleneindo-
linones, producing the 3,3 ′-spirocyclic oxindoles in high yields
and nearly perfect enantioselectivities ( Scheme 3 , 8aa−8na).
The enantioselective cyclization reactions of 6o−6r, which
contain 4-Cl, 4-F, 5-Cl, and 5-Br, on the indole ring,
respectively, were all converted to the corresponding products
in excellent yields with excellent enantioselectivities ( Scheme
3, 8oa−8ra). The N-protection of indole rings (N-Ac, N-Bz,
and N-CO
2Me) could be also utilized. In almost all of the
examples examined, 3,3′-spirocyclic oxindoles 8 were produced
in good chemical yields and good to excellent enantioselectiv-
ities ( Scheme 3 , 8sa−8ua). Various ethyl γ-benzyl allenoates
bearing o-, m-, and p-substituents in the phenyl rings were
suitable substrates, and the desired products 8 were isolated in
92−99% yields with 99% ee ( Scheme 3 , 8aa−8af). To further
investigate the substrate scope, the ester groups of γ-benzyl
allenoates were tested, and the yield slightly diminished when
we applied bulky steric tert-butyl γ-benzyl allenoates, retaining
excellent enantioselectivities ( Scheme 3 , 8ag−8ai).
We then examined the reaction scope with regard to catalyst
5a′, and the results are summarized in Scheme 4. The reaction
was well-tolerated with aryls of methyleneindolinones contain-
ing di ﬀerent para- and ortho-substituents, from electron-
donating to electron-withdrawing groups ( Scheme 4 , 8aa′−

were employed, respectively, the reaction could produce their
corresponding 3,3 ′-spirocyclic oxindoles in high yields and
excellent ee ( Scheme 4, 8va′, 8oa′−8ra′, and 8wa′). When we
used the methyleneindolinones containing N-Ac, N-Bz, and N-
CO
2Me protection, the substrates were all found to be suitable,
although slightly lower diastereoselectivities were obtained
(Scheme 4 , 8sa′−8ua′). Moreover, the phenyl ring at the γ-
benzylic position of allenoates could be replaced by other aryls.
Allenoates bearing an aryl moiety with meta and para
substituents were all found to be suitable in this transformation
(Scheme 4 , 8aa′−8ae′). Finally, we applied di ﬀerent ester
groups of γ-benzyl allenoates as substrates, and the
corresponding products could also be obtained with high
yield and excellent ee ( Scheme 4 , 8ag′−8ai′). The alkyl-
substituted methyleneindolinones (alkyl instead of Ar
1) were
also used as substrates to react with γ-benzyl-substituted
allenoates, and no product was formed.
In conclusion, we have developed a highly concise and
eﬃcient strategy for the construction of a new class of rigid P-
chirogenic phosphine catalysts, which are highly e ﬀective
catalysts for the asymmetric phosphine-catalyzed annulations
of γ-benzyl allenoates. To the best of our knowledge, this is the
ﬁrst systematic report on the phosphine-catalyzed asymmetric
(4 + 2) annulation of γ-benzyl allenoates. Both enantiomers of
the products could be obtained in good yields and with
excellent enantioselectivity through transformations that were
catalyzed by two diastereomers of Jia-Phos. Further application
of these catalysts to other transformations is underway.

Design of 1 ‑Phosphanorbornene Derivatives as Chiral
Organocatalysts for Enantioselective (4 + 2) Annulation Reactions of
γ‑Benzyl Allenoates
Siming Jia, Mengmeng Ma, Er-Qing Li, * Zheng Duan, * and Franc ̧is Mathey
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 3337 −3342 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: Two novel diastereoisomeric P-chirogenic phosphine catalysts, i.e., JiaPhos, which can be easily derived from
inexpensive and commercially available starting materials in ﬁve chemical operations (totally 4.16g scale), are introduced. To our
delight, the JiaPhos catalysts display good performance in enantioselective (4 + 2) annulations involving 3-methylene-2-oxindoles
and γ-benzyl allenoates, providing a wide range of 3,3 ′-spirocyclic oxindoles with good e ﬃciency and enantioselectivity.
P
hosphine-catalyzed reactions o ﬀer a very powerful tool for
the synthesis of structurally diverse optically active organic
building blocks. 1 As a result, the design of e ﬃcient chiral
phosphine catalysts has attracted much attention. 2 In the past
decades, many types of chiral phosphines have been developed
by Lu, 3 Zhao,4 Huang,5 Fu,6 Zhang,7 and other organic
chemists. 8 Although these phosphines showed excellent
catalytic activities in asymmetric phosphine catalysis, e ﬃcient
methodology for the design and synthesis of P-stereogenic
phosphines remains scarce. An early example with the
development of P-chirogenic catalysts was disclosed by the
Zhang group in 1997.
9 Subsequently, Sasai ’s group designed a
novel P-chirogenic catalyst with an o-hydroxyalkyl chelating
arm, which exhibited good performance in the aza-Morita −
Baylis−Hillman (aza-MBH) reaction.10 In 2014, Kwon and co-
workers developed a novel family of P-stereogenic [2.2.1]
bicyclic chiral phosphines, applying them in the asymmetric
installation of pyrrolines. 11 Recently, Zhang’s group reported a
novel class of cyclic phosphine-derived bifunctional phosphine
catalysts (Le-Phos), which showed high enantioselectivity in γ-
addition reactions of N-centered nucleophiles to allenoates
(Scheme 1, A).
12 As a part of our program, we set our goal to
de novo design novel P-stereogenic catalysts derived from the
1-phosphanorbornenes, in which three P −C bonds of the P-
chirogenic center are absolutely shackled. In addition, the two
alkyl groups link to the phosphorus atom that shows better
nucleophilic activity than 1-phosphanorbornadienes,
13 and
combining with a H-bonding site and multiple tunable side
chains, the de novo design of P-chirogenic catalysts (i.e.,
Jiaphos) may extend the applicative scope of asymmetric
phosphine catalysis to a greater extent ( Scheme 1 , B).
In 2003, Mathey and co-workers reported a Diels −Alder
reaction of 2 H-phospholes with trans-cinnamaldehyde.14 The
cycloaddition primarily took place at the C O bond, and only
minor C C bond adducts could be obtained. The
experimental results demonstrated that the carbonyl group of
aldehydes could compete with activated alkenes in (4 + 2)
cycloadditions. To our delight, when we applied trans-
cinnamaldehyde dimethyl acetal as a reactive substrate, the
cycloaddition completely took place at the C C bond,
aﬀording the desired compounds e ﬃciently. The phosphine
was then protected by further vulcanization. The mixture of
exo/endo-1 was obtained in a total of 61% yield, which could
be straightforwardly separated by column chromatography,
giving the exo-1 in 52% yield. Next, deprotection of exo-1 in
CH
2Cl2 at 0 °C produced the desired compound 2 (94%

In conclusion, we have developed a highly concise and
eﬃcient strategy for the construction of a new class of rigid P-
chirogenic phosphine catalysts, which are highly e ﬀective
catalysts for the asymmetric phosphine-catalyzed annulations
of γ-benzyl allenoates. To the best of our knowledge, this is the
ﬁrst systematic report on the phosphine-catalyzed asymmetric
(4 + 2) annulation of γ-benzyl allenoates. Both enantiomers of
the products could be obtained in good yields and with
excellent enantioselectivity through transformations that were
catalyzed by two diastereomers of Jia-Phos. Further application
of these catalysts to other transformations is underway.

value.title: Design of 1-Phosphanorbornene Derivatives as Chiral Organocatalysts for Enantioselective (4 + 2) Annulation Reactions of γ-Benzyl Allenoates

source_context.value: Graphical abstract summarizes the 5a/5a′ scope and antipodal products; it is not an extra experiment.
Scheme 1A depicts cited prior catalysts; Scheme 1B is design rationale for the current catalyst family, not a preparative experiment.
Single-crystal X-ray structures of 4d and 4d′ and CCDC accessions are characterization evidence, not separate syntheses.

Alkyl-substituted methyleneindolinones reacted with γ-benzyl allenoates gave no product; individual labels, quantities, and row-level conditions are not supplied, so no concrete control row is fabricated.
The article states SI exists, but no SI PDF was provided or explicitly associated in this session.
Pages 4–6 bibliography/prior-work citations are source context, not experiments of this paper.
